lem-dirichlet-normal-mixture-density-wel:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal P(\mathbb R)$ be the probability measures on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb R$, equipped with the evaluation sigma-algebra, and let $\sigma>0$.
For $F\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R)$ define
$$p_{F,\sigma}(x):=\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(x-z)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)F(dz).$$
Then $(F,\sigma,x)\mapsto p_{F,\sigma}(x)$ is jointly measurable,
$0<p_{F,\sigma}(x)\le(\sigma\sqrt{2\pi})^{-1}$ for every $(F,\sigma,x)$,
and $\int_{\mathbb R}p_{F,\sigma}(x)\,dx=1$. In particular it is the
Lebesgue density of the convolution of $F$ with $N(0,\sigma^2)$.
lem-hellinger-ratio-controls-kl-moments:
## Statement

Let $p,q$ be probability densities relative to one measure $\mu$, assume
$p\,d\mu\ll q\,d\mu$, let
$h^2:=\int(\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2d\mu$, and suppose
$R:=\operatorname*{ess,sup}_{q\,d\mu}(p/q)<\infty$, with $p/q=0$ on
$\{q=0,p=0\}$. Then $p\ll q$ and for a universal constant $C$,
$$\mathrm{KL}(p\,d\mu\Vert q\,d\mu)\le C h^2(1+\log^+R),\qquad \int p\left[\log(p/q)\right]^2d\mu\le C h^2(1+\log^+R)^2.$$
The logarithm is assigned value zero on $\{p=0\}$; the moment integrand is
also set to zero there.
lem-gaussian-convolution-kl-and-log-squa:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $p\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ be a nonnegative compactly supported probability density and suppose
$$ J:=\int_{\{p>0\}}\frac{(p''(x))^2}{p(x)}\,dx<\infty. $$
For $\sigma>0$, set $q_\sigma=p*\phi_\sigma$, where $\phi_\sigma$ is the centered normal density with standard deviation $\sigma$. Then
$$ \int\frac{(p-q_\sigma)^2}{q_\sigma}\,dx\le\frac49\sigma^4J,\qquad \mathrm{KL}(p\Vert q_\sigma)\le\frac49\sigma^4J,\qquad \int p\left[\log\frac p{q_\sigma}\right]^2dx\le\frac49\sigma^4J. $$
The logarithmic integrands are zero where $p=0$. No unimodality or uniform bound on $p/q_\sigma$ is assumed.
lem-dirichlet-normal-mixture-finite-supp:
## Statement

There is a universal constant $C$ such that, for $A,\sigma>0$,
$0<\eta<1/2$, and every probability measure $F$ supported on $[-A,A]$,
there is a discrete probability measure $F'$ on $[-A,A]$ with at most
$$C(A/\sigma\vee1)\log(e/\eta)$$
support points and
$$\|p_{F,\sigma}-p_{F',\sigma}\|_1\le\eta,\qquad
\|p_{F,\sigma}-p_{F',\sigma}\|_\infty\le\eta/\sigma.$$
lem-iid-posterior-contraction-under-coun:
## Statement

Assume AC. For each $n$, let $\Pi_n$ be a prior on a measurable parameter
space $\Theta_n^*$, and let $p_\theta$ be a jointly measurable family of finite-valued densities
against one sigma-finite measure, and let $p_0$ be the true density for IID
data $X_1,\ldots,X_n$. Let $\epsilon_n,\delta_n>0$ satisfy
$\delta_n\le\epsilon_n$, $n\delta_n^2\to\infty$, and
$n\epsilon_n^2\to\infty$. Suppose for a constant $C_0>0$ that
$$\Pi_n\!\left\{\theta:\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_\theta)\le\delta_n^2,\quad
P_0\left[\log\frac{p_0}{p_\theta}\right]^2\le\delta_n^2\right\}\ge e^{-C_0n\delta_n^2}.$$
Let $S_n\subseteq\Theta_n^*$ be a measurable sieve with
$\Pi_n(S_n^c\mid X_{1:n})\to0$ in $P_0^n$-probability. Partition it into
countably many measurable sets $S_{n,j}$, put $\pi_{n,j}=\Pi_n(S_{n,j})$,
and let $N_{n,j}=N(\epsilon_n,\{p_\theta:\theta\in S_{n,j}\},h)$ be the
finite covering number as defined in [[def-covering-packing-bracketing-number-and-metric-entropy]], with centers in that density class, whenever $\pi_{n,j}>0$. If
$$e^{-n\epsilon_n^2}\sum_{j:\pi_{n,j}>0}\sqrt{N_{n,j}\pi_{n,j}}\longrightarrow0,$$
then for every sufficiently large fixed $M$, the posterior mass of
$$\{\theta:h(p_\theta,p_0)>M\epsilon_n\}$$
converges to zero in $P_0^n$-probability.
lem-dirichlet-normal-mixture-sieve-entro:
## Statement

For $A\ge1$, $\tau>0$, and $0<\epsilon<1/4$, let
$$\mathcal P_{A,\tau}:=\{p_{F,\sigma}:F([-A,A])=1,\ \tau\le\sigma\le2\tau\}.$$
There is a universal constant $C$ such that
$$\log N(\epsilon,\mathcal P_{A,\tau},h)\le C(A/\tau\vee1)\left[\log\!\left(\frac{C(A/\tau\vee1)}{\epsilon}\right)\right]^2.$$
The same bound, with a changed universal constant, holds for
$$\mathcal P_{A,\tau,\rho}:=\{p_{F,\sigma}:F([-A,A]^c)\le\rho,\ \tau\le\sigma\le2\tau\}$$
whenever $0\le\rho\le c\epsilon^2$ for a sufficiently small universal $c>0$.
Here $N$ is the covering number in the stated metric.
lem-dirichlet-normal-mixture-countable-b:
## Statement

Let $0<a_2<a_1<1$, $n^{-a_1}\lesssim\sigma_n\lesssim n^{-a_2}$, and
$\gamma>1$. Suppose $G$ is a probability measure on $(0,\infty)$ satisfying
$G((0,s])\le C e^{-\beta s^{-\gamma}}$ for all sufficiently small $s>0$.
Let $s_n\to0$ with $s_n/\sigma_n\to\infty$. For integers $j$ with
$2^j\sigma_n\le s_n$, put $\widetilde r_n:=\min\{r_n,1/4\}$ and
$$\mathcal P_{n,j}:=\{p_{F,\sigma}:F([-A,A]^c)\le\widetilde r_n^2/8,
\quad 2^j\sigma_n\le\sigma<2^{j+1}\sigma_n,\quad \sigma\le s_n\},$$
and let $\pi_{n,j}$ be the prior mass of the corresponding parameter band,
so $\pi_{n,j}\le G([2^j,2^{j+1}))$. Suppose $r_n>0$ and, for some fixed
sufficiently large $M_0$ and fixed $\eta>\gamma/[2(\gamma-1)]$,
$$r_n\ge M_0\max\{(n\sigma_n)^{-1/2}\log n,
n^{-1/2}\sigma_n^{-\eta}\}.$$
With $N_{n,j}=N(r_n,\mathcal P_{n,j},h)$, one has
$$e^{-nr_n^2}\sum_{j:2^j\sigma_n\le s_n}\sqrt{N_{n,j}\pi_{n,j}}\longrightarrow0.$$
If instead $G$ is supported on a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$, the same
conclusion holds under the first rate term alone.
lem-dirichlet-process-simplex-small-ball:
## Statement

Assume AC, let $\alpha$ be a finite nonzero measure of total mass $m$, and
let $F\sim DP(\alpha)$. Consider a finite partition
$(U_0,U_1,\ldots,U_N)$ with $\alpha(U_0)=0$ or
$0<\alpha(U_0)\le m$. Write $\alpha_j=\alpha(U_j)$ for $j\ge1$, and assume
$$a\eta^b\le\alpha_j\le1\quad(1\le j\le N),\qquad 0<\eta<1/4,qquad N\eta\le1/4,$$
for fixed $a,b>0$. For every $w=(w_1,\ldots,w_N)$ in the probability
simplex, there are constants $c,C>0$ depending only on $a,b,m,\alpha(U_0)$
such that
$$\Pr\!\left\{\sum_{j=1}^N|F(U_j)-w_j|+F(U_0)\le3\eta,\quad
\min_{1\le j\le N}F(U_j)\ge\eta^2/2\right\}\ge C\exp\{-cN\log(e/\eta)\}.$$
When $\alpha(U_0)=0$, the zero-base cell has $F(U_0)=0$ almost surely and is
omitted from the Dirichlet vector.
lem-dirichlet-normal-mixture-local-prior:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $p_0$ be a bounded probability density supported on a compact
set $K\subset\mathbb R$. Let $\alpha$ be a finite nonzero measure with a
continuous density bounded below by a positive constant on a neighborhood of
$K$. Assume
$$h(p_0,p_0*\phi_\sigma)\le C\sigma^2$$
for all sufficiently small $\sigma>0$, where $\phi_\sigma$ is the centered
normal density with standard deviation $\sigma$. Let $F\sim DP(\alpha)$ and
let $S\sim G$ be independent, where $G$ is any probability measure on
$(0,\infty)$. Suppose $n^{-a_1}\lesssim\sigma_n\lesssim n^{-a_2}$ for
$0<a_2<a_1<1$. Set $\sigma=\sigma_nS$ and
$$\delta_n:=\max\{(n\sigma_n)^{-1/2}\log n,\ \sigma_n^2\log n\}.$$
Then, for some constant $C_1>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$,
$$\Pi_n\!\left\{(F,\sigma):\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_{F,\sigma})\le C_1\delta_n^2,\quad
P_0\left[\log\frac{p_0}{p_{F,\sigma}}\right]^2\le C_1\delta_n^2\right\}
\ge e^{-C_1n\delta_n^2}.$$
Here $p_{F,\sigma}$ is the density of [[lem-dirichlet-normal-mixture-density-well-defined]],
and all logarithmic integrands are set to zero on $\{p_0=0\}$.
lem-dirichlet-normal-mixture-interval-ma:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $p_0\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ be a probability density with compact support $K$, a finite union of intervals. Suppose $J=\int_{\{p_0>0\}}(p_0'')^2/p_0<\infty$ and there are $a,c>0$ such that $P_0(I)\ge c\lambda(I)^a$ for every interval $I\subseteq K$. Let $F\sim DP(\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is a finite nonzero measure with continuous strictly positive density on a neighborhood of $K$, and independently let $S\sim G$ for any probability measure $G$ on $(0,\infty)$. Suppose $n^{-a_1}\lesssim\sigma_n\lesssim n^{-a_2}$ for $0<a_2<a_1<1$, and put $\sigma=\sigma_nS$. Then for constants $C_1,C_2>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$,
$$ \Pi_n\left\{\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_{F,\sigma})\le C_1\sigma_n^4,\quad P_0\left[\log\frac{p_0}{p_{F,\sigma}}\right]^2\le C_1\sigma_n^4\right\}\ge\exp\{-C_2\sigma_n^{-1}(\log n)^2\}. $$
Consequently, for $d_n=\max\{(n\sigma_n)^{-1/2}\log n,\sigma_n^2\}$, the same two local quantities are at most $C_1d_n^2$ on a set of prior mass at least $e^{-C_3nd_n^2}$. Logarithmic integrands vanish where $p_0=0$.
lem-dirichlet-normal-mixture-posterior-s:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $p_0$ be supported on a compact interval $I=[L,U]$ with
$L<U$, let $F\sim DP(\alpha)$ for a finite nonzero base measure whose
density is bounded below on a neighborhood of $I$, and let $S\sim G$ be
independent with $\sigma=\sigma_nS$. Put $R=(U-L)/2$ and, for $d>0$,
$I_d=[L-d,U+d]$.
Observe IID data from $p_0$ under the location-mixture density
$p_{F,\sigma}$. Let $\epsilon_n,\delta_n>0$ with
$n\epsilon_n^2\to\infty$ and $n\delta_n^2\to\infty$. Suppose the local KL
and log-square prior-mass condition gives a denominator event
$$P_0^n\{D_n\ge e^{-C_0n\delta_n^2}\}\longrightarrow1,$$
where $D_n=\int\prod_i p_{F,\sigma}(X_i)/p_0(X_i)\,\Pi_n(dF,d\sigma)$.
Choose $s_n\to0$ and put $q_n=2\Phi(-R/s_n)$, where $\Phi$ is the
standard normal distribution function. If
$$nq_n-(C_0+2)n\delta_n^2\to\infty,\qquad
n\epsilon_n^{-2}s_n^{-1}e^{-d^2/(2s_n^2)}\to0,$$
then the posterior complement of
$$\mathcal S_n:=\{(F,\sigma):\sigma\le s_n,\ F(I_d^c)\le\epsilon_n^2\}$$
converges to zero in $P_0^n$-probability.
thm-dirichlet-normal-mixture-posterior-c:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $p_0$ be a finite-valued probability density on $\mathbb R$
with compact support. Assume $p_0\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ and, with the
integrands set to zero on $\{p_0=0\}$,
$$\int_{\{p_0>0\}}\left[\left(\frac{p_0''}{p_0}\right)^2+
\left(\frac{p_0'}{p_0}\right)^4\right]p_0\,dx<\infty,$$
and assume there is $C<\infty$ such that
$$h(p_0,p_0*\phi_\sigma)\le C\sigma^2$$
for all sufficiently small $\sigma>0$. Here $h$ is the root-L2 Hellinger
distance of [[def-hellinger-distance-between-density-laws]], and
$\phi_\sigma$ is the centered normal density with standard deviation
$\sigma$. Let $F\sim DP(\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is a finite nonzero
measure with a continuous, strictly positive Lebesgue density on an open
interval containing $\operatorname{supp}(p_0)$, and independently let
$S\sim G$ on $(0,\infty)$. For $\sigma=\sigma_nS$, define
$$p_{F,\sigma}(x)=\int\phi_\sigma(x-z)F(dz),$$
and observe $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ IID from $p_0$. Suppose
$$n^{-a_1}\lesssim\sigma_n\lesssim n^{-a_2},\qquad
0<a_2<a_1<1,\qquad a_2\ge(4+\gamma)^{-1},$$
and, for some $\beta>0$ and $\gamma>1$,
$$G((0,s])\lesssim e^{-\beta s^{-\gamma}}\ (s\downarrow0),\qquad
G((s,\infty))\lesssim e^{-\beta s^\gamma}\ (s\to\infty).$$
Here $u_n\lesssim v_n$ means $u_n\le Cv_n$ eventually for a fixed
constant $C$. For every fixed
$\eta>\gamma/[2(\gamma-1)]$, put
$$\epsilon_n=\max\left\{(n\sigma_n)^{-1/2}\log n,
n^{-1/2}\sigma_n^{-\eta},\ \sigma_n^2\log n\right\}.$$
Then for every sufficiently large fixed $M$,
$$\Pi_n\!\left(h(p_{F,\sigma},p_0)>M\epsilon_n\mid X_{1:n}\right)
\longrightarrow0$$
in $P_0^n$-probability. If $G$ is compactly supported in $(0,\infty)$,
the middle term $n^{-1/2}\sigma_n^{-\eta}$ may be omitted. The conclusion
is only in probability; it supplies no almost-sure contraction or generic
minimax-optimality assertion.
cor-dirichlet-normal-mixture-interval-ma:
## Statement

Under the hypotheses of [[thm-dirichlet-normal-mixture-posterior-contraction]],
assume additionally that $\operatorname{supp}(p_0)$ is a finite union of
intervals and there are $a,c>0$ such that $P_0(I)\ge c\lambda(I)^a$ for
every interval $I$ contained in the support. Then the source's sharpened
Hellinger contraction rate is
$$\max\{(n\sigma_n)^{-1/2}\log n,\ n^{-1/2}\sigma_n^{-\eta},\ \sigma_n^2\},\qquad \eta>\frac{\gamma}{2(\gamma-1)}.$$
If $G$ is compactly supported in $(0,\infty)$, the middle term is omitted.
